name: cap-capability-packaging-implement
description: How to build capability packaging on this stack: the filesystem adapter that runs today, a registry adapter that changes where the bytes come from and what identity means, the migration off directories that are rendered and checked in place, where a package resolution is wired so the platform's guarantees ride on it, and the conformance run that decides whether either source may serve. Load it when writing or reviewing the resolver, when a component is about to join a path to find a package, when someone asks 'where does loading actually happen', 'can we serve these from a registry without touching the core', or 'why did this package resolve here and not there', and before recording any packaging conformance result as passing.

purpose.text: Build what cap-capability-packaging specifies: two package sources chosen by configuration, one conformance run that resolves the same identities through both and diffs them, and the wiring that makes a package resolution a recorded step rather than an unobserved file read. build-adapter-pair owns why there are two.
purpose.quote: the second exists to prove the first is not load-bearing

shapes.name: package-source-binding (proposed shape; the migration procedure and the wiring table are in references/implementation-notes.md)

enum: a namespace-scoped name with a content digest

shapes.name: packaging-conformance-report (proposed shape; the per-package rows are in references/implementation-notes.md)

invariants.text: cap-capability-packaging owns the contract (F-b3-07, F-b3-01) and the right-hand columns are what prove the layout replaceable. This skill adds only how it is built: an implementation that makes a third frontmatter field required, adds a fourth load tier, or resolves an identity its binding record does not describe has produced a defect, not an extension.
invariants.quote: The right two columns prove it is swappable.

invariants.text: build-adapter-pair states the swap test (F-meta-04). The consequence here is that both sources are selected by a binding record read as configuration: if choosing between a directory and a registry requires editing a file the core owns, the boundary is drawn wrong and the pair has found the defect it exists to find.
invariants.quote: If Part B cannot swap an implementation without touching the core, the boundary is drawn wrong

invariants.text: build-adapter-pair states rule 4 (F-b1-05). The consequence here is that the packages this platform publishes are plain conformant directories that a third party loads with their own runtime, so integrating with our capabilities never means importing a loader of ours.
invariants.quote: If integration requires our SDK, a boundary is bespoke where a standard existed

invariants.text: agentic-stack states design rule 7 as a test (F-b1-08, F-b4-01). What this skill adds: a package resolution is a step like any other, so it is recorded with the correlation attribute set at dispatch and counted against the unit's ceiling, and there is no flag by which a caller can load a package unobserved.
invariants.quote: Telemetry, policy, provenance and budget are applied by the platform, not requested by the caller

invariants.text: build-evidence-record states the labelling rule (F-part-c-08). The consequence here is that 'both sources resolve the same packages' is claimed until a run is attached naming the command, the identity set, the code version and the counts.

Apply build-adapter-pair: this pair's differing axes (where_bytes_come_from, identity_is) are recorded in the adapters section below and in the second adapter's swap_procedure; this row does not restate them. Two bindings identical on every axis are one adapter written twice and fail the pair check. proposed pointer, see that skill.

not_exposed.text: Proposed: cap-capability-packaging already owns this exclusion for the distribution transport and the on-disk path; applied at the pair level, which source served a resolution is visible only as the resolution outcome's source and digest members, never as a difference in the package a caller receives.

instructions.action: Put every package source behind the binding record and keep path joins, network clients and archive readers inside the adapter directory; core and seam modules import the capability's operations only.
instructions.why: agentic-stack states design rule 1 as a test (F-b1-02), and a hard-coded package root is that failure in executable form: it is a product decision about where bytes live, written into code that is supposed to be indifferent to it.
instructions.quote: The core imports interfaces, never implementations

instructions.action: Build today's adapter as a thin wrapper over a directory scan: enumerate the configured roots, read each package's frontmatter, expose the four operations, and translate a missing file or a missing required field into a resolution outcome rather than raising the runtime's own exception.
instructions.why: PASS.md records this adapter as already in place as skill files, so the work is not writing a loader but confining one; translating at the wrapper's edge is what stops a file-not-found becoming the platform's failure contract.

instructions.action: Build the second adapter against a registry entry format: resolve a namespace-scoped identity, fetch the package as an addressable artifact, verify its content digest before anything is read, and cache it locally. Fill in both execution-model axes in its binding record.
instructions.why: build-adapter-pair owns why a second adapter exists (F-b1-04). The consequence here is specific: a second directory layout would let the interface keep assuming a local path, while a fetched, digest-verified package is what forces identity and integrity to become contractual.
instructions.quote: supports both git and OCI distribution

instructions.action: Proposed migration: the packages in this repository are directories rendered from data and checked in place. Publish the same trees through the registry adapter, resolve every identity through both sources, and require identical resident fields, bodies, reference sets and digests before any directory stops being the source of truth.
instructions.why: Proposed: the migration risk is not that the registry fails loudly but that it serves a stale or re-rendered copy that differs in one reference file; a digest diff over the whole identity set is what turns that into a list instead of a surprise. Research query: is there a recorded migration record (kb/ceremonies or an evidence record) from another capability in this platform that ran a shadow resolver or a diffed cutover the same way, confirming this is the platform's own established migration pattern rather than invented here?

instructions.action: Wire resolution on the load path: record every resolution with the correlation attribute the platform sets at dispatch, consult policy before a package from a namespace the platform does not own is loaded, and count the load against the unit's ceiling.
instructions.why: agentic-stack states that the cross-cutting guarantees are applied and not requested (F-b1-08); a package that can be loaded without a record is a capability that entered the system without one.
instructions.quote: The platform applies each; a caller cannot decline them.

instructions.action: Write one conformance run parameterised over the binding records: resolve the same identity set through every configured source, assert the spec-conformance counters per source, and diff the resolved packages across sources.
instructions.why: build-adapter-pair owns the rule that every interface ships with two adapters (F-b1-04); the consequence here is that one run over two sources is what makes the swap a tested property rather than a plan, because a per-source suite would let each source define conformance as whatever it happens to do.
instructions.quote: Every interface ships with at least two adapters

instructions.action: Have each adapter report the source and digest it actually resolved and compare them against its binding record at start-up; a mismatch fails the definition of done for that source.
instructions.why: build-definition-of-done requires the effective configuration to be attested rather than assumed, because configuration written in the documented place has been observed to take no effect at all (F-a7-04).

instructions.action: Proposed: open references/implementation-notes.md when running the migration diff, wiring the load path, or reviewing a binding record. The body of this skill is enough to build and judge the pair without it.
instructions.why: Proposed: the migration procedure and the wiring table are longer than the body's budget and are needed only while doing those two jobs.

best_practices.text: build-definition-of-done already states the green-gate finding (F-a7-03). What this skill adds: make packages_checked an assertion and not a log line, because a conformance run pointed at an empty or mistyped root scans nothing, finds nothing wrong, and exits 0 - the same shape of green as a pipeline whose behavioural stages were all skipped.

Proposed: check the rendered package, never the data that produced it. Packages here are generated, so a conformance run that reads the generator's input will pass while the artifact a runtime actually loads is stale or malformed. Research query: is there a recorded conformance run comparing a rendered package against its generator input on this repository, confirming this check was actually built rather than only recommended?

Pin an explicit version on every published package rather than relying on ordering by publication time, since a registry that cannot parse a version falls back to ordering by when it was published, which makes a republish silently reorder resolution.
best_practices.quote: Non-semantic versions are allowed but will be ordered by publication timestamp.

adapters.maps_to: the four operations served by scanning package directories under a configured root on the local filesystem, reading frontmatter in process. PASS.md records the adapter only as skill files; describing it as a filesystem directory layout is the manifest's entry and is proposed here.
adapters.cannot: Proposed: cannot verify that two copies of a package are the same, because its identity is a path and it produces no digest; cannot serve a runtime that has no access to the tree.
adapters.swap_procedure: Change the binding record's resolution and location, restart, confirm the reported source and digest match the record, then run the conformance run over the same identity set. No core file is edited.

adapters.maps_to: the same four operations served by a registry entry format with namespace-scoped identity, distributed as an addressable artifact and verified by content digest before use.
adapters.cannot: Proposed: cannot hand back a mutable local path, cannot be edited in place between runs, and cannot serve a package whose only identity is a directory name - so anything it cannot implement was a filesystem assumption that had leaked into the contract.
adapters.swap_procedure: Its binding record differs from today's on where_bytes_come_from (network fetch versus local directory read) and on identity_is (a namespace-scoped name with a content digest versus a path). One parameterised conformance run covers both, and the pair stays claimed until that run is recorded.
adapters.quote: supports both git and OCI distribution

definition_of_done.expected: The gate (27 checks) and the conformance run together prove: one portable package directory resolves through the same interface from a filesystem source and a content-addressed registry source, discovery reads only the resident tier, the two required resident fields (name, description) are enforced by the interface itself rather than per adapter, a package missing one is refused as a typed document-invalid problem, and the swap is proven by an equal case count with the source and digest axes differing (adapters_run=2). Earlier criterion named tools/conformance_capability_packaging.py, replaced by the harness on 2026-09-03.
definition_of_done.breakage: Widen REQUIRED_RESIDENT in harness/capability-packaging/interface.py from ("name", "description") to ("name", "description", "owner") and change nothing else (the harness README's breakage); restore with git checkout -- harness/capability-packaging/interface.py.
definition_of_done.expected_failure: Every fixture package, including the well-formed one, is now missing the invented required field: discovery, resolution and every dependent tier fail, and the conformance run drops from 12/12 to 2/12 cases passed and reports conformance FAILED, exiting non-zero — the green run can fail, and the interface enforces exactly the two fields the spec requires, never more.
definition_of_done.quote: A criterion nothing can fail is not a criterion

open_questions.question: Which source is the default when the platform starts?
open_questions.evidence: Measure, over the full identity set, resolution latency for a cold start under each binding and the failure mode when the registry is unreachable at the moment a package is first needed.
open_questions.default: The directory adapter, because it needs no process beyond the caller to make progress; the registry adapter stays a conformance-run peer and a publication target until the measurement says otherwise.

open_questions.question: Does loading a package spend the calling unit's ceiling, or the platform's?
open_questions.evidence: Count, over a run of the reference consumption example, how much of a unit's ceiling is consumed by resolutions rather than by work, and whether any unit is terminated by resolution cost alone.
open_questions.default: Charge it to the calling unit, since every unit of work carries a ceiling and exceeding it terminates the unit rather than the platform; revisit if resolution cost alone ever terminates a unit.
open_questions.quote: Every unit of work carries a ceiling
